programmes.d: Lawyer Al (Dan Duryea) and brother Frank (Dick Foran) turn to robbing banks and trains after Union troops raid their home.
An Old West gunfighter (Hal Holbrook) turns a young farmer (Jeff Osterhage) into a justice fighter with a special gun.

programmes.t: The New Daughters of Joshua Cabe
programmes.d: A framed sheriff (John McIntire) is about to hang, but his bogus wayward daughters have a plan.
A British scout (Kevin Dillon) infiltrates a French stronghold near the Great Lakes during the 1750s.
A bank robber (Fred MacMurray) takes a new name in another town and falls for the lawyer-sheriff's (Lin McCarthy) sister (Dorothy Green).
An Arizona rancher (Randolph Scott) protects his empire from a rival landowner (Richard Boone) and his hired guns.
The new marshal (Fred MacMurray) is the only one in town who thinks a charming killer (Robert Vaughn) should hang.
A dispute between stage lines ends with a steel-armored stagecoach.
A cavalry sergeant (Broderick Crawford) leads soldiers, civilians and an Indian (Johnny Stewart) on a desert trek.
The fastest gun (George Montgomery) in Texas is let out of prison to help the Rangers stop a gang of outlaws.
A Chicago hotel desk clerk (Jack Lemmon) talks a trail boss (Glenn Ford) into taking him on a cattle drive to Mexico.
A new lawman (Bill Elliott) punches out cattle rustlers who like to shoot sheriffs.
Three trappers become scouts for a cavalry captain (Guy Madison) who loses his fort to a hated colonel (Robert Preston).
Absent from Custer's Last Stand, an Army captain (Randolph Scott) volunteers for the Little Bighorn burial detail.
A stagecoach driver seeks to capture "The Monk," a notorious highwayman, in order to clear himself.

programmes.t: The Gun That Won the West
programmes.d: Superior Springfield rifles help scouts (Dennis Morgan, Richard Denning) and the cavalry get forts built in Wyoming.
